title: Vision Plans Contact-Lens Orders — Filing Limit and Binder-Based Retroactive Coverage
content:
**Question and answer for the member services desk — contact-lens orders on the Vision Plans**

**Q. In what order are timeliness and coverage decided for a contact-lens order?**
A. The first of the following that holds governs:
1. The claim reached Cascade more than the filing limit after the date of service — 180 calendar days at a participating location, 365 calendar days out of network. The order is denied for timely filing. At a participating location the member owes nothing for it; out of network the member keeps the whole receipt.
2. Otherwise, the enrollment still stands applied, and the latest binder payment the funding billing account received meets all three conditions: it was not returned, it is for at least the plan unit's monthly premium for its coverage tier, and it was received on or before the binder deadline. The latest binder payment is the account's latest payment with payment purpose binder in the Premium Billing Accounts records. The binder deadline is the coverage effective date plus 30 calendar days, and a payment on the deadline day is in time. A service dated on or after the coverage effective date is then settled under the contacts rules, coverage having started retroactively on that date.
3. In every other case the enrollment's own status and dates decide. The order is settled under the contacts rules only when the enrollment is active or terminated and the date of service is on or after its coverage effective date and on or before its termination date when it has one. Otherwise its lines are denied as not eligible and the member pays the whole retail charge.

**Q. What counts as a returned binder?**
A. A binder payment that a returned-payment entry on the billing account names.

**Q. Where do the limits fall exactly?**
A. Day 180 (participating) and day 365 (out of network) after the date of service are in time, and the next day is late. A binder on the 30th day after the coverage effective date is in time, and on the 31st it is not. A binder equal to the monthly premium of the unit's tier suffices; a smaller one does not.

**Q. Hypothetically, a contact-lens order dated before the coverage effective date, on an applied enrollment with a timely full binder?**
A. Case 2 covers only services dated on or after the coverage effective date. The enrollment's own status then decides, and it still stands applied, so the order is denied as not eligible.
